_comment: Shared cross-language pin for the IFCPROXY an IFC4X3 alignment or positioning product becomes below IFC4X3 (#7683, EXPORT-MERGE-8): a minted GlobalId, source attributes 1 to 6 kept verbatim, the quoted source type in ObjectType when that slot is $, then .NOTDEFINED.,$. Run by rust/export/tests/schema_upconvert_parity.rs (product_proxy_vectors_agree_with_the_shared_fixture_7683) and packages/export/src/schema-upconvert-sweep.parity.test.ts. The two twins mint the GlobalId differently (Rust from the express id, TypeScript from the source line), so both sides replace the proxy's GlobalId with <MINTED> before comparing and separately assert it is not the source one. The first two lines are the records the adversarial review found detached on Railway_Railway_project_simple_IFC4X3 (#22) and Viadotto_Acerno (#159981).

cases.why: Railway #22: Name, OwnerHistory, ObjectPlacement and Representation survive; ObjectType was $, so it names the source type
Viadotto_Acerno #159981: a referent keeps its placement and representation; PredefinedType has no IfcProxy slot
an authored ObjectType is kept, not overwritten with the type name
the same rule on an IFC2X3 target, for one of the four alignment types that were always proxied
